title: Build houses to the building code (NCC Volume Two and the Housing Provisions)
what: Carry out building work on houses and other Class 1 and 10 buildings in accordance with the Building Code of Australia (NCC Volume Two and the Housing Provisions, with the NSW variations), a condition of every development consent and complying development certificate for building work. Energy standards for homes are set by BASIX instead of the code's. The edition in force is NCC 2022 until NCC 2025 is adopted on 1 May 2027. Its schedule in NCC 2025 varies 53 national provisions.

assessment.summary: Work must meet the National Construction Code (Volume Two and the Housing Provisions) as New South Wales applies it. The code sets minimum safety, health, amenity, accessibility and energy standards, whose benefits are not weighed here; meeting and certifying them adds to the cost of every project.

marks.reason: Designing, documenting and certifying each project against the code adds cost, and the state's own variations add to it for builders who work in several states.

assessment.confidence_note: Marked to agree with the NCC adoption records (burden -1); the Productivity Commission finds several code changes were adopted although their impact analyses showed a net cost. No evaluation of the requirement itself was found.
